observations: Full-length damaged echo 600000e010 and header-like echo 020000e010 followed by 020400fa at 20 ms are accepted with one TX by the original module.
Exact echo followed by reply bytes at 20/23/26/29 ms is accepted by the original module.
No echo with 020400fa at 20 ms fails in the original module; Android AUTO/NONE direct-frame acceptance is an explicit compatibility behavior.
The original wrong-target case fails. Reply at 95 ms after an 80 ms configured timeout fails.
The original short-echo, invalid-checksum and trailing-noise probes timed out in isolated workers and were terminated; these outcomes are inconclusive.
The original concatenated two-frame probe was accepted despite a 4-byte declared length with payload 00fa020400. Android strict total-length/extra-data checks intentionally reject that input.
FE followed by entry has TX offsets 54.9 ms for exact echo, 54.2 ms damaged echo and 81.7 ms absent FE echo in the scripted probe.
limitations: The scripted UART data and arrival delays are supplied test inputs, not captured ECU recordings.
The FTDI handle is mocked, so these results establish native receive/parsing behavior rather than physical FTDI/K-Line signal correctness.
An inconclusive worker timeout is not evidence of acceptance or rejection.
Original acceptance of malformed combined replies is not a requirement to reproduce unsafe/lax parsing in Android.
The Java fixtures use deterministic 6 ms TX completion and 7 ms echo arrival to reproduce Android scheduling; those times are synthetic and separate from observed native read timestamps.

android_completion_boundary.evidence_type: Android design choice tested with synthetic memory UART data; not an original Lite runtime observation
android_completion_boundary.rationale: Wait three 8 ms FTDI latency intervals after a candidate complete frame, using the same quiet interval as wake cleanup, to detect fragmented trailing data or a frame-shaped prefix followed by a second reply.
android_completion_boundary.deadline_bound: The quiet guard remains bounded by the selected transaction RX deadline; a complete candidate received before the deadline may finish at that boundary.
android_completion_boundary.physical_limit: This checks additional UART bytes observed within the bounded receive window. It does not establish that the physical ECU sent a valid reply, prove the cause of damaged echo, or guarantee that no later bytes can arrive beyond the transaction deadline.
